source.title: One Word at a Time: Incremental Completion Decomposition Breaks LLM Safety
source.authors: Samee Arif; Nai-Hao Deng; Zhijing Jin; Rada Mihalcea

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures projections onto a difference-in-means refusal direction during its own jailbreak attacks and relates those measurements to attack trajectories. It does not ablate or add the direction, so this is a conceptual test of whether attacks suppress the direction, not a direct reproduction of the original causal intervention.
record.gate_note: The paper estimates a refusal direction from refusal-response and benign-completion activations, then reports attack-related projection results. ASR tables that do not measure the refusal direction are not included as rows. The paper also measures projections onto a separately estimated safety direction; those results are recorded under fits_no_version because they do not establish that harmfulness judgment is separately encoded from refusal.
record.test_reason: The study builds a difference-in-means refusal direction (harmful/refusal vs Alpaca/benign hidden states, following Arditi et al.). It then measures whether a new multi-turn jailbreak (ICD) lowers projections onto that direction relative to RAW prompting, in Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-3-12B. This bears on V3 in a new attack setting. It is observational only: there is no ablation, addition or adversarial training, so it is not a T1/T2 reproduction of the causal claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors say their mechanistic analyses 'suggest' ICD succeeds by shifting representations away from refusal- and safety-aligned states. In the Limitations they say the directions capture specific trends and are not complete predictors of behaviour.
record.recipe_differences: The study estimates a refusal direction by difference of mean activations and measures its projections during attacks, but uses refusal responses versus benign completions and does not intervene by ablating or adding the direction.
record.method_sensitivity: Projection patterns vary by model, attack variant, layer, and trajectory length. Gemma-3-12B shows a final-layer exception to its late-layer suppression pattern; Llama-3.1-8B projection ordering between AUTO and SEED also changes with trajectory length.

fits_no_version.finding: ICD variants also lower projections onto a safety direction built from judge-labelled harmful vs safe responses. At Gemma's final layer this reverts to positive for RAW, AUTO and SEED.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Incremental-completion jailbreaks shift hidden states away from an output-derived safe-continuation direction as well as a refusal direction.

record.problems: The mechanistic evidence is qualitative projection analysis and does not establish causality through a refusal-direction intervention. The authors state that the estimated directions are not complete predictors of behavior. The reported paired confidence intervals and significance tests concern ICD-PREFILL versus PREFILL attack success, not the refusal-direction projections.
record.rows_left_out: Attack-success rates and their paired comparisons were not included because they do not themselves measure refusal-direction suppression. No other results bearing directly on the tested version were left out.

untested.parts: Causal claim that suppressing the direction produces the jailbreak (no ablation, no addition, no restoring the direction to block the attack). No training against the direction's ablation or robustness test.
No ablation or addition of the direction; no capability check.
DeepSeek-R1-distilled models get ASR only; no direction measurement.

missing.what: The standard PREFILL (single-turn prefill attack) baseline also suppresses the refusal projection in Gemma late layers; reported order is ICD-PREFILL > PREFILL > ICD-AUTO > ICD-SEED > RAW.
Layer-selection procedure: the layer is chosen as the one maximising the absolute RAW-vs-ICD difference. This should be recorded as a condition on all R rows.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T2 to T3: a new attack setting with observational projection evidence on V3. The reader's limits_scope label for Gemma layer 47 was based on ordering between attack variants, which is irrelevant to V3; all attacks remain below RAW there. It is replaced by a limits_scope on the weak link between projection and ASR. The projections appear to be averaged over all trajectories, not only successful ones, despite the 'successful trajectories' framing. The direction uses 50 JailbreakBench vs 50 Alpaca prompts, framed as refusal-response vs benign-completion states.

versions.untested_parts: No projection-ablation or direction-addition intervention; no test of whether other abilities are preserved.
No weight-edit removal of the direction.

The paper measures refusal-direction projections during attacks but does not causally suppress the direction; it does not train against direction ablation or test whether such training adds robustness.
No test of whether refusal is better described by an affine subspace, cone, or multiple refusal directions.
The paper measures a safety direction and a refusal direction separately, but does not test whether harmfulness judgment is encoded separately from the refusal decision.
The paper evaluates attack success across model families, but does not test transfer of the refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or training stages.
The paper evaluates some reasoning-distilled models for attack success, but does not measure or intervene on the refusal direction in reasoning models.

relationships.reason: Refusal-direction projections fall from high positive under RAW to negative under all ICD variants, most strongly for ICD-PREFILL (R1–R3). The evidence is qualitative and observational only.
relationships.display_finding: All ICD variants changed strongly positive RAW refusal projections to negative values, with the largest observational shift under ICD-PREFILL.

relationships.condition: Gemma-3-12B, ICD-AUTO/SEED/PREFILL, layers 40–46 and final layer 47
relationships.reason: All attack variants push refusal projections negative in late layers and stay negative at layer 47, where RAW returns positive (R4–R6).
relationships.display_finding: All attack variants produced negative late-layer refusal projections that remained negative at layer 47, where RAW projections returned positive.

relationships.condition: Relating projection size to attack success across variants and trajectory lengths
relationships.reason: Refusal projection does not track success closely. Llama n=4: near-identical refusal projections but different ASR (R1, R2). Gemma layer 47: the strongest attack (ICD-PREFILL) is the least suppressed (R6). Authors say the directions are not complete predictors.
relationships.display_finding: Llama at n=4 showed nearly identical projections with different attack success, while Gemma's strongest attack, ICD-PREFILL, was least suppressed at layer 47, making the directions incomplete predictors.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Relating projection size to attack success across variants and trajectory lengths
source_check.reason: The label is right, but the reason misreads Llama n=4: ASRs there are 71.73% vs 71.54%, so the projections and ASRs both nearly match, and the n=4 mismatch is in the safety direction. Better evidence: at Llama n=3, AUTO has the more negative refusal projection but SEED the higher ASR. At Gemma layer 47, ICD-PREFILL (highest ASR) is the least suppressed ICD variant but the most suppressed in layers 40-46, a layer-choice dependence. Gemma AUTO projects lower than SEED at all k but SEED has slightly higher ASR at k=1 and k=7. The Limitations section says the directions are not complete predictors.

relation.reason: The study reports its own measurements of whether successful attack trajectories lower the refusal-direction projection relative to RAW. This bears directly on V3's attack clause.

tranche.reason: The direction is a difference-in-means one following Arditi et al. (from refusal responses vs benign Alpaca completions, not harmful vs harmless instructions). The study measures projections onto it under a new multi-turn jailbreak (ICD) on Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-3-12B: a new setting with a result on V3. It is not an exact T1 replication, and it does not use a different method on the same question (T2).

source_check.notes: All projection evidence is qualitative from figures, with no stated values. It is measurement only, with no ablation or addition, and the layer is chosen to maximise the RAW-vs-ICD difference. The l2 reason and V3.against[9] should cite Llama n=3 instead of n=4. It is unclear whether RAW itself dips negative in Gemma layers 40-46: the text says RAW 'returns positive' at the final layer.

statements.correction: If named: in the multi-turn ICD attack, the refusal-direction projection goes from positive under RAW to negative. Llama-3.1-8B: Fig 3a, layers 23-24. Gemma-3-12B: layers 40-47. Figure-only, no stated numbers, measurement only.
statements.problem: The statement cites R1 and R4 from this study but never names it and gives no numbers for it. Nothing it says contradicts the study.

statements.correction: Llama-3.1-8B, n=3: ICD-AUTO has the more negative refusal projection, but ICD-SEED has higher ASR. n=4: refusal projections nearly identical, ASR AUTO 71.73% vs SEED 71.54%; SEED has lower safety projections. Gemma-3-12B, layer 47: ICD-PREFILL (highest ASR) is more positive than ICD-AUTO and ICD-SEED. It is still negative while RAW is positive, and it is the most negative across layers 40-46. Authors: 'the final layer alone may not fully capture refusal behavior'. Also Gemma: AUTO projects lower than SEED at all k, yet SEED has slightly higher ASR at k=1 and k=7.
statements.problem: The Llama n=4 point is misread. At n=4 the ASRs are 71.73% vs 71.54%, nearly equal, so near-identical refusal projections go with near-identical ASR. The mismatch the authors flag at n=4 is in the safety projection. The Gemma point is right only among the ICD variants.

statements.correction: Llama-3.1-8B: ICD-PREFILL has the most negative refusal and safety projections (Fig 3). ASR: PREFILL 75.96%, ICD-PREFILL 83.85-87.31%.
statements.problem: None. The study does have no base-model control. Its only comparison condition is plain PREFILL (prefill without the ICD trajectory).

statements.correction: Add: ICD projections stay negative at layer 47 too. ICD-PREFILL is most negative in layers 40-46 but more positive than ICD-AUTO and ICD-SEED at layer 47. The layer is chosen as the one with the largest absolute RAW-vs-ICD difference.
statements.problem: Accurate, but it leaves out the actual layer-dependence the study reports.
The visible (truncated) text cites no rows and makes no specific claim about this study. Its general claims fit this study's Llama and Gemma results.
